items.text: Amazon opened its largest AI data center on 1,200 acres in Indiana, hosting half a million AWS Tranium 2 chips to support Anthropic, an OpenAI competitor. Just over a year ago, the area was farmland, but now seven buildings are operational, with plans for around 30 total. The center will use 2.2 gigawatts of electricity, enough for over a million homes. Locals express concern about the impact on utilities , water, and roads, and Amazon is funding upgrades and improvements. This rapid buildout is unusual, but Amazon emphasizes its expertise in large-scale AI infrastructure. The company designs and uses its own Tranium chips rather than Nvidia GPUs, allowing cost efficiency and high compute capacity. Anthropic benefits from this partnership as Amazon provides scalable AI training infrastructure. Despite criticism about overbuilding and potential inefficiencies, the project demonstrates how major tech firms can quickly deploy custom AI hardware at an industrial scale. The site is part of a broader multi-campus AI expansion in the United States. Difficult words: utility (a service that provides something useful to people, usually public services like electricity, water, gas, or internet), expertise (special knowledge or skill in a particular area; knowing how to do something very well), scalable (able to increase in size or capacity easily). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Amazon built a huge AI data center in Indiana on 1,200 acres. The site uses 500,000 Tranium 2 chips to run AI for Anthropic. One year ago, the land was farmland, but now seven buildings work, and there will be about 30 buildings when complete . The center will use a lot of electricity and water. Locals worry about roads, water, and electricity, so Amazon pays for improvements . The company uses its own chips instead of Nvidia, which lowers costs. This allows fast AI training for Anthropic. Amazon can build many data centers quickly and provide large computing power. The project shows how technology companies create AI infrastructure and train models at a very large scale . Difficult words: complete (having all parts or done fully), improvements (changes that make something better or work more effectively), scale (the size or level of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amazon is building a very big AI center in Indiana. The center is on a large farm area. It has many special chips called Tranium 2. These chips help Anthropic, a company which works with AI. Before, the land has only corn and fields. Now seven buildings work, and there will be 30 buildings later. The center needs a lot of electricity and water. People in the town worry about roads, water, and electricity. Amazon pays money to fix them. The company uses its own chips, not Nvidia chips, so it can save money. The center shows how a big company can build many AI machines fast and help AI companies train computers. Difficult words: chip (a small part which makes computers work), fix (to repair or make something work correctly), train (to teach). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A police raid in Rio de Janeiro targeting the Red Command drug gang left at least 64 people dead, including four police officers. The large-scale operation took place in the poor areas of Complexo do Alemão and Penha, involving helicopters, armored vehicles, and hundreds of officers. Authorities said 81 suspects were arrested and large amounts of drugs and weapons were seized. Rio’s governor described the operation as the biggest in the city’s history. However, human rights organizations and the UN condemned the violence, calling for investigations into possible abuses. Critics said such raids are often inefficient, as they target low-level members rather than gang leaders. The clashes caused chaos in Rio, with buses burned and schools closed. Experts described the death toll as war numbers, showing how violent Brazil’s drug conflict has become. Difficult words: large-scale (very big in size or involving many people or things), condemn (to say strongly that something is bad or wrong), death toll (the number of people who die in an event, like a war or accident). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A big police raid in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, killed 60 suspects and four police officers. The police attacked the Red Command gang in two poor areas called favelas. They used helicopters and armored cars and arrested 81 people. Police also took many guns and drugs. The city’s governor said it was the biggest operation in Rio’s history. Human rights groups and the United Nations said the violence was too much and asked for checking what happened. Many people were scared as buses burned and schools closed. Experts said the raid will not stop the gangs because police often arrest small criminals, not the big bosses. Difficult words: raid (a sudden attack by police or soldiers), suspect (a person police think did a crime), armored (covered with strong metal to stay safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Police in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, fight a big drug gang . Many people die — 60 men and 4 police officers. The gang lives in favelas. Favelas are poor areas with small houses. They use cars, helicopters, and many guns. They take some people and find a lot of drugs. Some people go to the hospital. The boss of Rio de Janeiro says that it is the biggest police job ever. People in the city feel scared . Some schools close and buses burn. The United Nations and Human rights groups say that this fight is bad. They want the police to explain what happens. Difficult words: gang (a group of people who do illegal things together, like sell drugs or steal), poor (having little money or basic things like food or a home), scared (afraid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A wedding video from Iran has caused a major political controversy. The footage shows the daughter and wife of Rear Admiral Ali Shamkhani, a senior Iranian official, wearing Western-style clothes without hijabs. This sparked anger because ordinary Iranian women face harsh punishments for similar behavior under strict Islamic laws. Shamkhani, who once led Iran’s National Security Council during the protests over Mahsa Amini’s death, is accused of hypocrisy, demanding modesty from citizens while his own family ignores these rules. The case highlights a deep double standard within Iran’s ruling class, where powerful figures live freely while others suffer. Many Iranians criticized Shamkhani online, but he dismissed the backlash and blamed Israel for leaking the video. The story reflects a broader pattern seen in many countries, where politicians control women’s choices in public but allow different rules for themselves and their families. Difficult words: hypocrisy (pretending to have moral beliefs that one does not follow), double standard (different rules for different groups), backlash (a strong negative reaction from many people to something that has happened or been said). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A wedding video in Iran made many people angry. It shows the daughter and wife of Ali Shamkhani, a top Iranian leader, wearing Western clothes and no hijabs . This upset Iranians because women in Iran must wear hijabs or face punishment . People called Shamkhani a hypocrite because he tells others to follow Islamic rules, but his family doesn’t do it. He was also in power when Mahsa Amini died after the police arrested her for not wearing a hijab correctly. Many people protested, but the police were very harsh. Now, people say the rich and powerful in Iran have one rule and other people have another. Difficult words: hijab (a headscarf that many Muslim women wear to cover their hair in public), punishment (something bad that happens to someone because they broke a rule or law), hypocrite (a person who says one thing but does another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A video from Iran shows a wedding. The bride and her mother do not wear a hijab . The bride’s father is a very important man in Iran. He tells all women to wear hijabs, but his family does not do it. Many people are angry. They say that it is not fair. Poor women must follow the rules, but rich people can do what they want. Some people remember Mahsa Amini. The police take her because she does not wear her hijab properly. She dies. Many people protest. The police hurt them. People want all women in Iran to be free. Difficult words: bride (a woman who is getting married), hijab (a scarf which many Muslim women wear to cover their hair), poor (having little money or not enough to live well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dahbia Benkired, a 27-year-old woman from Algeria, received a life sentence without parole for raping, torturing, and killing 12-year-old Lola Daviet in Paris in 2022. It is the first time in French history that such a sentence has been given to a woman. During the trial, Benkired showed no emotion, even when shown photos of her victim. Experts said she had no mental illness but described her as cold and lacking empathy . She said she was indifferent when asked about the murder. The crime shocked France and started a political debate because Benkired was in the country illegally. The court heard about her difficult past, including childhood violence, abuse, and drug use, but the jury still found her fully responsible. French law allows a review of such sentences after 30 years, but only under very strict conditions. Lola’s family expressed deep sadness during the verdict and said they wanted justice for their daughter. Difficult words: parole (permission to leave prison early), empathy (ability to understand others’ feelings), indifferent (not caring or showing any feelings about something), debate (a discussion where people express different opinions about an important topic). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A French court gave 27-year-old Dahbia Benkired life in prison for killing 12-year-old Lola Daviet in 2022. She attacked and killed the girl in Paris. Benkired came from Algeria and lived in France illegally; she had no documents to stay in France. During the trial , she stayed quiet and didn’t show any feelings. Experts said she was not mentally sick but had no empathy for others. The murder shocked many people in France and made politicians talk about rules for immigrants. The court can look at her case again after 30 years, but only if it is safe. Lola’s family cried during the verdict and said it was not fair to send her to prison for the rest of her life. Difficult words: trial (a legal process in court), mentally (connected to the mind or thinking, not the body), empathy (understanding other people’s feelings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman named Dahbia Benkired goes to prison for the rest of her life. She kills a 12-year-old girl, Lola, in Paris. Dahbia is from Algeria. She lives in France without official documents. In court , she says little and looks cold . She is not sorry for the little girl. Many people in France are sad and angry. They talk about rules for people who come from other countries. The judge says Dahbia cannot go out of prison. Maybe after 30 years, judges can look at her case again. Lola’s family is very sad and cries in court. Difficult words: court (a place where people decide about a crime or another legal situation), cold (when somebody shows no feelings or kindness), judge (a person who decides in court). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Flippy 2 is an AI robotic fry station developed by automation company Miso Robotics in California, US. The robot completes all the tasks of cooking fried food for fast food restaurants, so it removes much of the human work. The machine also can cook different meals simultaneously , which removes the need for catering staff, and it hurries the drive-through process. Flippy 2’s robotic arm is similar to a machine in car plants, and cameras and AI power its manufacturing. When an order comes, the robot automatically receives instructions, it takes a frozen product, fries it for the precise amount of time, and puts the finished product in a box. According to Miso’s CEO, the robot works faster, more accurately, more reliably, and happier than most humans. Positions at frying stations are the hardest to fill and retain , so the robot doesn’t take workers’ jobs. People are delighted to have the help, so they can do other tasks. Difficult words: automation (the use of machines and computers instead of people to do a job), simultaneously (at the same time), retain (to keep or continue to have). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In California, US, Miso Robotics developed a robot which works in fast food restaurants. At first, the robot only turned burgers, but workers soon realized that it could do more tasks. Now, the robot does several tasks at once. For example, it prepares french fries or onion rings. When an order comes, a worker sends instructions to the robot. The robot uses special arms that look similar to those in car factories. The robot’s advantage can do many tasks at the same time, which saves a lot of time and work. The robot uses AI and cameras and is faster than humans. It prepares meals for the right amount of time, and people are happy that they don’t have to do the work, especially at night. Difficult words: instruction (directions to do something), advantage (a thing which makes something special or interesting), AI (when a computer controls another computer or robot). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In California, US, company Miso Robotics makes a special robot. The robot helps in restaurants. The robot has arms. Robots in car factories have similar arms. At first, the robot only turns burgers. Workers think that the robot can do other things, too. Now, the robot makes french fries, fried onions, and other meals. A computer controls the robot. The robot works faster than people. It can do more tasks at the same time. The robot knows exactly when the food is ready. The robot does tasks which nobody wants to do. Workers are happy that somebody does this demanding work. The work is easier for them at night. Difficult words: control (to have power over something), exactly (right), demanding (very difficult). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Why do we say “God bless you” when someone sneezes? People cannot say exactly when or where the response started; however, we have some theories. A long time ago, people thought that when someone sneezed, snot and the soul escaped, too, and to say “God bless you” was to help. Another theory is from the 6 th century when a plague struck Europe, and Pope Gregory I formally ordered people shout out blessings to protect someone who sneezed. Similarly, in the 14 th century during the bubonic plague , sneezing was a sign that a person might be sick with the plague. Today, the reaction is mostly ingrained , and people think it is polite. However, people don’t use it worldwide. For example, in Spanish speaking countries, people say “salud”, which can be translated to “good health”. Difficult words: snot (liquid that comes from someone’s nose when he has a bad cold or sneezes), bubonic plague (the most common type of plague in humans), ingrained (firmly established and difficult to change). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When someone sneezes, in some countries, people say “God bless you.” Nobody really knows the start of this response, but people have several theories about it. In the past, when someone sneezed, people thought that his soul left the body. All they could saw was “God bless you.” In the 6 th century, a plague happened in Europe, and Pope Gregory I ordered people to give blessings to someone who sneezed. In the 14 th century, another plague happened, and a person who sneezed could be sick. People started to say, “God bless you.” These days, for many people, the response is a natural reaction, and many think that it is polite to say it. In some countries, people don’t say it. For example, in Spanish language countries, people say the word “salud.” It means something like “good health”. Difficult words: theory (a set of ideas to explain something), plague (a dangerous disease which spreads quickly and kills many people), blessing (God’s help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People sometimes sneeze when they have a cold. Or they sneeze when something bothers their nose. Their nose gets full. Suddenly, air comes from their nose and mouth. People usually say “God bless you” when someone sneezes. Some countries say other things. In Spanish language countries, people wish good health when someone sneezes. Nobody really knows why people say, “God bless you.” People have some ideas about it. In the past, a plague happens in a lot of the world. People are scared. The disease is very dangerous. Someone who sneezes is sick. People ask God to keep him safe from the plague. These days, people say these words normally. For many people, it is polite . Difficult words: bless (to ask God to keep someone safe), plague (a dangerous disease which makes many people sick and kills many people), polite (good behavior with others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Profits at Porsche fell sharply this year, dropping by almost 96% in the first nine months of 2025. The German carmaker blamed the fall on its new strategy to move away from electric cars and return to producing more petrol and hybrid vehicles. The company delayed the launch of several electric models after facing weak demand, especially in China, where the luxury car market has slowed down. This restructuring cost billions of euros, and parent company Volkswagen took a 5-billion-euro hit to support the changes. Porsche also faces higher costs from tariffs on exports to the US, as it doesn’t have a factory there. A new CEO, Michael Leiters, will take over in January to help rebuild sales, focus on top-end products, and regain investor confidence. Difficult words: blame (to say that someone or something caused a problem or mistake), hybrid (something made from two different things), top-end (very expensive and high-quality). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Porsche lost almost all of its profit in 2025, around 96%. The company changed its strategy and decided to make more petrol and hybrid cars instead of electric ones. The reason is that people don’t buy many expensive electric cars, especially in China. The change cost the company a lot of money, and Volkswagen, which owns Porsche, lost about 5 billion euros. Porsche also pays more because of tariffs in the United States. Sales in China fell by about 25%, and many jobs in the car industry are in danger. A new boss will start in January to try to improve the situation and bring back strong sales. Difficult words: profit (the money a company makes after paying all its costs), strategy (a company’s plan or idea for success), hybrid car (a car which uses both petrol and electric power to move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Porsche is a famous car company from Germany. It makes less money this year. The company loses 96% of its profit . People do not buy many electric cars. Porsche wants to make more petrol and hybrid cars again. It costs a lot of money to change the plan. In China, people buy fewer cars now. Volkswagen, the big company that owns Porsche, loses money too. Porsche also pays extra money because of tariffs in America. A new boss will start soon to help the company and make more sales. Difficult words: profit (the money which a company makes after it pays all its costs), hybrid car (a car which uses both petrol and electricity to move), tariff (a tax which a government puts on things coming from another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some Russians are turning away from coffee, which they see as a Western import, and returning to their traditional love of tea. Andrei Kolbasinov, founder of the Nitka teahouse chain, wants to bring back the country’s old tea culture that disappeared after the 1917 Revolution. His teahouses recreate the atmosphere of pre-revolutionary Moscow, when tea houses were popular gathering places. Today, his growing business reflects a wider cultural shift as Russia becomes more inward-looking and embraces national traditions instead of Western trends. While tea remains a staple drink in most Russian homes, the recent political tensions with the West have made it a symbol of cultural identity. Despite import challenges caused by sanctions, Nitka sources tea from allies such as China and Georgia. The revival of tea culture mirrors Russia’s search for self-sufficiency and nostalgia for its past. Difficult words: embrace (to accept or welcome something new or different), staple (something that is used or needed very often), nostalgia (a warm, sad feeling when remembering the past). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Russia, some people now prefer tea instead of coffee because they see coffee as a Western drink. A businessman, Andrei Kolbasinov, opened a chain of teahouses called Nitka. He wants Russians to enjoy tea again like they did before the 1917 Revolution. His teahouses look old-fashioned and offer a calm place for people to meet. The change also shows how Russians focus more on their own culture and less on Western ideas after problems with the West. Many Russians still drink tea at home with jam or lemon. Some tea comes from China and Georgia because sanctions make trade with other countries difficult. Difficult words: chain (a group of stores which one company owns), old-fashioned (not modern, something from the past), sanction (a rule which limits business or contact with a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people in Russia drink tea again. They drink less coffee because coffee comes from the West. A man named Andrei has tea shops . The name of his shops is Nitka. He wants people to drink tea like long ago, before big changes in Russia. In his shops, people can sit, talk, and feel warm. Many people in Russia drink tea at home with jam and lemon . Some tea comes from China and Georgia. It is not easy to buy tea from other countries now. Russians like tea because it feels more Russian. Difficult words: tea shop (a small place where people can drink tea and sometimes eat cakes or snacks), lemon (a yellow fruit with a sour taste). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indian news channels were once respected for supporting democracy, but now many viewers in India and neighboring countries see them as propaganda tools. Reporters in places like Nepal and Bangladesh have been criticized or even attacked for pushing pro-India or pro-Modi narratives rather than reporting facts. Critics say Indian TV focuses on sensationalism , nationalism, and religious bias, rather than balanced journalism. This has led to growing anti-India feelings across South Asia. Experts argue that these channels harm India’s image abroad by spreading false or exaggerated stories, often to support political agendas. Inside India, the problem is even worse: journalists face lawsuits, arrests, and censorship. Most media outlets are now owned by business or political allies of the government, reducing independence. The result is a serious credibility crisis, with Indian news often seen as noisy entertainment rather than real journalism. Difficult words: propaganda (information used to influence people), sensationalism (making news shocking to attract attention), credibility (how believable something is). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Indian news channels used to be trusted and respected, but today many people see them as political tools. In Nepal and Bangladesh, people accuse Indian reporters of showing only the Indian government’s view. Critics say the news focuses on drama, religion, and politics, not on truth. This makes many people in nearby countries dislike India’s media. Inside India, journalists have many problems. Some lose jobs or face police because they criticize leaders. Many TV stations belong to business people who support the government, so reporters cannot work freely. Because of this, Indian news looks more like noisy shows than real information. Difficult words: trusted (someone or something you believe is honest and reliable), accuse (to say someone did something wrong), criticize (to say that something is bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indian TV news is good in the past. But now, many people do not trust it anymore. In Nepal and Bangladesh, people say that Indian reporters do not tell the truth . They say that Indian news helps the government and not the people. On TV, there is a lot of shouting and talk about politics and religion . Many people do not like this. In India, some reporters cannot say what they think. The government and rich people have control of many TV stations. So, the news is not free and honest. Difficult words: truth (something real or correct), religion (believing in a god), control (to have power over someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Physical fitness seems to be becoming an important image tool for politicians. In Poland, President Karol Nawrocki’s gym videos showing him boxing and lifting weights have attracted wide attention. He follows a global trend of leaders showing athletic strength — from Putin’s judo to Obama’s basketball. Some athletes, such as Vitali Klitschko or Arnold Schwarzenegger, have even successfully moved into politics. According to Professor Jacek Wasilewski from the University of Warsaw, physical power can help politicians appear strong and reliable, especially in uncertain times. People naturally associate a muscular body with safety and leadership. Wasilewski adds that modern politics is more emotional and visual, using images of fighters or heroes to connect with ordinary people. While former Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s footballing image was seen as friendly, Nawrocki’s boxing projects determination and courage — traits that help him appear as a protector and leader. Difficult words: muscular (having strong, well-developed muscles), determination (strong will to do something), courage (bravery). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

More and more politicians show their fitness to look strong. Polish President Karol Nawrocki often posts gym videos where he lifts weights and boxes. Other leaders, like Putin and Obama, also like to show their sports skills. Some athletes, like Arnold Schwarzenegger or Vitali Klitschko, later became politicians. Professor Jacek Wasilewski says that people often trust strong leaders because they look powerful and safe. He explains that when life feels uncertain, voters prefer politicians who look like fighters. Nawrocki’s boxing looks brave and serious , while Donald Tusk’s football seems friendly but not powerful. Showing fitness can help politicians get more support . Difficult words: brave (not afraid of anything), serious (not funny), support (help or agreement). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many politicians like sports. Polish President Karol Nawrocki shows his gym videos online. He lifts weights and boxes. Other leaders, like Putin and Obama, also play sports. Some sportsmen, like Arnold Schwarzenegger, become politicians later. A professor from Warsaw says that strong people look safe and good for the country. When people feel afraid, they like strong leaders. Nawrocki looks strong when he boxes. Tusk plays football, but it looks more like fun. People think Nawrocki is brave and powerful . Sport helps politicians look strong and win votes. Difficult words: weight (a heavy object which people exercise with at the gym), brave (not afraid of anything), powerful (strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heineken, the world’s second-largest brewer, warned that its beer sales will drop in 2025 due to global economic problems. The company lowered its previous forecast again, saying that demand remains weak, especially in Latin America and Europe. CEO Dolf van den Brink said that the company expects demand to improve once economic conditions stabilize. Analysts noted that although results were not strong, they were slightly better than expected. Heineken’s shares rose 1% after the announcement. Despite facing challenges such as lower beer consumption, competition from alcohol alternatives, and growing health awareness, Heineken reported market share gains in Brazil, Mexico, and Vietnam. The company’s revenue fell 0.3% in the third quarter, but that was still above expectations. Overall, the results show that while Heineken continues to struggle with slow sales, investors remain cautiously optimistic about future recovery . Difficult words: revenue (money a company gets from selling things or services), cautiously (carefully), recovery (a return to a better or stronger situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Heineken says it will sell less beer in 2025 because people are buying less. The company changed its plan again after seeing weak demand in Europe and Latin America. Its boss, Dolf van den Brink, says things will get better when the economy becomes more normal. Even if sales go down, some analysts think the news is not as bad as they expected. Heineken’s shares grew a little after the report. The company also got a bigger market share in Brazil, Mexico, and Vietnam. It made a bit less money than before, but did better than many thought. Heineken still hopes for a recovery later. Difficult words: demand (how much people want to buy something), share (a small part of a company which people can buy or sell), recovery (a return to a better or stronger situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heineken is the second biggest beer company in the world. It says that it will sell less beer next year. People buy less because money is a problem in many countries. The boss says that the situation can get better soon. Heineken sells beer in Europe, Brazil, Mexico, and Vietnam. In some places it sells more, in others less. People drink less alcohol these days. The company makes a little less money now, but it is not too bad. People who study business think that Heineken can do better in the future. Difficult words: beer (an alcoholic drink from water, barley, and hops), study (to look at something, learn about it, and understand it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Unilever is delaying the spin-off of its Magnum Ice Cream division because the US government shutdown has stopped official reviews of new stock listings . The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) cannot process the necessary registration statement, so the company must wait before listing the Magnum Ice Cream Company in Amsterdam, New York, and London. The delay shows how the shutdown, now in its third week, is disrupting global business and could cost the US economy up to 15 billion dollars a week. Other companies, such as DeepGreenX, have also had to cancel or postpone listings. Unilever will keep a 19.9% stake in its ice cream business, which also includes Ben & Jerry’s and Cornetto. Investors say the delay is not a major issue because the company’s long-term growth and market position remain strong despite the temporary setback . Difficult words: spin-off (creating a new company from part of another one), listing (when a company’s shares are put on a stock exchange so that people can buy and sell them), setback (a problem or delay that stops progress or makes something take longer). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Unilever cannot start its new Magnum Ice Cream company now because the US government shutdown stopped important work. The US market office, called the SEC, cannot check the company papers, so Unilever must wait. The ice cream company wanted to start selling shares in Amsterdam, New York, and London in November. But the delay is not a big problem, and Unilever says it will continue later this year. The company will still own about 20% of the business. The shutdown is already hurting other companies and the US economy. But Unilever’s investors say they are not worried because they believe the company is strong and will grow in the future. Difficult words: shutdown (when the government stops work), share (a small part of a company), delay (when someone or something is late). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Unilever wants to make a new ice cream company called Magnum Ice Cream Company. It wants to sell parts of it in Amsterdam, New York, and London. But now. Unilever cannot do it. The US government shutdown stops many offices from working, and Unilever must wait. SEC is a company which checks important papers. SEC cannot work now. Unilever must wait. Unilever is not worried. It will start the plan later. People who give money to Unilever think the company is strong and will grow. Difficult words: shutdown (when the government closes and stops work), office (a place where people work), plan (what you want to do in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A robot that is able to burrow through grain could help save millions of tons of food waste every year. The Crover robot is able to go 10 meters beneath grain storage silos and report on moisture and humidity levels. A tiny sensor on the robot watches conditions in real-time, and it sends information to farmers via a smartphone app. Long-term grain storage is laborious, dangerous, and easy to make mistakes. When grain isn’t stored correctly, temperature and moisture start to grow. As a result, bugs start to breed, and mycotoxins and fungus start to grow in the grain, which means a total loss to a farmer. An estimated 630 million tons of grain are lost in storage every year on a global scale. The robot could help save grains and human lives, too. Difficult words: burrow (to dig a hole or tunnel through the ground or something solid), silo (a tall tower that farmers use to store grain), mycotoxin (a toxic substance that a fungus makes). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Farmers are using a special robot that goes through their grain. Farmers store grain in special towers, and the work is very demanding . If the grain gets wet, it gets warmer. More bugs come, and dangerous fungi start to grow in the grain. It is not possible to use such grain for food, and it means a big loss for farmers. Reports say that farmers all over the world must throw away around 630 million tons of grain. The robot could change this problem. It moves through the grain, and its little sensor checks the temperature and moisture of the grain. It sends information to a farmer’s phone, and he immediately knows if everything is okay. Difficult words: demanding (a task which requires a lot of time and energy), fungus (a special living thing that gets its food from old food or other living things), moisture (how wet something is). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Farmers do a lot of hard work. They keep grain in special towers. The towers can be more than 10 meters high. The work is not easy to look after the grain. Farmers must keep the grain dry. It must not get too warm. If the grain gets wet or warm happens, bugs come. Fungi start to grow. People can’t eat this grain. Farmers throw it away. It costs them a lot of money. Farmers all over the world throw away around 630 million tons of grain every year. A special robot can help. It moves through the grain. It checks how warm and wet it is. It sends information to a farmer’s phone. Farmers can look after the grain better. The Louvre Museum in Paris was closed after a dramatic robbery early on Sunday morning. According to France’s culture minister, three masked thieves entered the museum through a freight lift that was being renovated. They reached the Apollo Gallery, which holds France’s remaining crown jewels, broke the windows, and stole several valuable pieces of jewelry before escaping on scooters. Reports say they used chainsaws to get inside. Police are now investigating, and the museum has been closed. The exact number of stolen items and their total value are still unknown, but they include jewelry once owned by Empress Eugénie, wife of Napoleon III. Experts say the theft is one of the most serious and daring crimes ever to happen at the Louvre. The robbers took advantage of ongoing renovation work to enter the building unnoticed. Difficult words: freight (goods or things that are carried by a truck, train, ship, or plane), daring (brave or risky), take advantage (to use a situation to get what you want, often cleverly or unfairly). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: robbery (stealing from a place or a person), crown jewels (jewels and crowns which belong to a country’s royal family), bold (brave). Until the 3 rd century AD, the town of Baia was the most coveted destination for wealthy Roman citizens, senators, and emperors. Now, it’s hidden beneath the sand and pebbles in the waters of the Gulf of Pozzuoli, just a few kilometers from Naples, Italy, and the only residents are fish and seahorses. The slow movement of land from volcanic activity caused the land to submerge , and in 1969, divers discovered the ruins of two marble statues by chance. About 15,000 divers, snorkelers, and tourists visit the site all year round to travel back in time and swim through ancient streets, mosaics , statues, and the remains of a seaside resort. Over the years, archeologists have moved some of the ancient objects above the sea to protect them from rock-eating plants and animals, strong tides, and thieves. However, the archeologists have placed copies of the originals underwater so that divers can experience the city as it was 2,000 years ago. Difficult words: covet (to want something very much), submerge (to go under water), mosaic (small pieces of stone or glass that are arranged together to make a picture or pattern). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Volcanic activity in the Italian Gulf of Pozzuoli meant that the land started to move towards the sea. Over the centuries, the sea flooded the streets, houses, and statues, and in 1969, divers discovered them again. The divers found pieces of two statues, but they did not know that there was a whole town in the sea. Archeologists are people who study old things. Archeologists took some of the things out from the sea because plants and animals destroyed them. Archeologists then put copies of the same things back in the sea. This means that tourists and divers can still come and swim through the old streets and see how the town looked 2,000 years ago. Difficult words: emperor (the man who was the leader or king of ancient Rome), divers and snorkelers (people who swim very deep and people who swim in the top of the water with tools to help them breathe), volcanic activity (when gas and lava come out from the earth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: ancient Rome (a large area in Southern Europe, Northern Africa, and a part of Asia, which is from 2,000 years ago), diver (a person who swims deep in the water), mosaic (small pieces of stone or glass, which make a bigger picture). Greenland, the world’s largest island, holds huge deposits of valuable minerals known as rare earths, which are essential for technologies like smartphones, electric cars, and rockets. Although mining remains limited, companies such as Critical Metals plan to extract these resources from the southern region. China currently controls most of the global supply, but the US and Europe are eager to secure their own sources. Greenland’s strategic Arctic location and its mineral wealth have sparked major international interest, including from the US government. However, mining in Greenland is expensive and difficult because of its icy, remote landscape and lack of infrastructure. Local communities hope new projects will bring jobs and development, though many remain concerned about environmental impact. With three of the world’s largest rare earth deposits, Greenland could soon become a key player in global mineral production. Difficult words: deposit (a natural collection of minerals in the ground), essential (very important or necessary), remote (far away from cities or towns; difficult to reach). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Mining there is hard because it is far, cold, and has little transport. Some local people hope it will bring new jobs and money. Others worry about the environment. The world is watching because Greenland may become an important place for these valuable materials. Difficult words: supply (an amount of something what people can use), mine (a place where people dig in the ground to get metals, coal, or other minerals), valuable (worth a lot of money or very important). IKEA’s annual sales dropped for the second year in a row as the furniture giant continued lowering prices to attract customers struggling with high living costs. The company cut prices by around 10% over the past two years after previously raising them during the pandemic. Despite a 1% decline in global sales to 44.6 billion euros, the number of products sold and store visits increased, showing that shoppers are buying more low-cost items. CEO Jon Abrahamsson Ring said IKEA can focus on long-term decisions because it is not listed on the stock exchange and wants to support consumers whose confidence has weakened. In the US, prices rose on some items due to tariffs, though IKEA is trying to absorb the extra costs. Ingka Group, IKEA’s largest franchisee , also reported a 1.6% sales decline but remains cautiously optimistic about future recovery. Difficult words: absorb (to take in or handle something difficult), franchise (a business that has permission to use another company’s name, products, and system), cautiously (carefully and without taking big risks). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

IKEA’s boss, Jon Abrahamsson Ring, said the company can plan for the long term and wants to help customers who have less money. In the US, IKEA raised some prices because of high tariffs , but it tries to pay some of the extra cost itself. Ingka Group, the main IKEA partner, also had a 1.6% drop in sales but hopes for better times soon. Difficult words: long term (over a long period of time, not just for now), franchise (a business that has permission to use another company’s name, products, and system), tariff (a tax on imported things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of people in Iași, Romania, attended the annual Saint Parascheva pilgrimage , one of the largest in the country. The pilgrimage lasts eight days and culminates on 14 October, the saint’s feast day. Devotees lined up for kilometers in the rain and cold, showing their devotion to pray before the saint’s relics . Many pilgrims expressed that witnessing the relics brought them joy and a sense of calling. The cathedral and city center were decorated with flowers under the theme ‘Symphony of the Lily,’ including 58,000 chrysanthemums in various colors. Volunteers worked to ensure the area was visually beautiful for visitors. Saint Parascheva’s relics have a long history, traveling across Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria, and finally arriving in Iași in 1641. The Romanian Orthodox Church canonized her in 1955, setting 14 October as her feast day. Last year, around 300,000 visitors came to see the relics, and this year the Church expects a similar number. The celebration combines faith, history, and community participation. Difficult words: pilgrimage (a journey to a holy place), culminate (to reach the highest point or the final stage of something), devotee (a person who strongly loves or supports something, often in religion), relic (an object connected to a saint), canonize (to officially declare someone a saint). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: pilgrimage (a journey to a special place where people speak to their god), feast (a special meal or celebration, often for a holiday or festival), relic (an object connected to a saint). Madagascar faces political turmoil as President Andry Rajoelina goes into hiding after an assassination attempt. Weeks of nationwide protests, mainly led by young demonstrators called ‘Gen Z Mada,’ demanded his resignation due to issues like unemployment, corruption, and the high cost of living. The protests escalated when an elite army unit joined, intensifying pressure on the president. Rajoelina dissolved the national assembly and dismissed his government, appointing only a few ministers. In a Facebook broadcast, he confirmed he left the country for safety but didn’t reveal his location, leaving citizens uncertain about who governs the country. Opposition leaders now aim to impeach him, but they need to convince ruling party MPs to proceed. The unrest stems from long-standing problems that the president failed to resolve over his years in power. People demanded better access to basic services, but the movement expanded to call for leadership change. The political future remains uncertain as the opposition seeks to organize elections and a transitional government . Difficult words: turmoil (a situation with a lot of confusion, problems, or chaos), elite (a small, powerful, or important group of people), impeach (to formally accuse a leader of wrongdoing), transitional government (a temporary government that rules until a new official government is ready). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Opposition groups try to convince members of the ruling party to remove him. People first want better water and electricity, but now they want the president to leave. They are worried about the future of the country and hope for a new government and elections soon. Difficult words: resign (to leave a job or position), national assembly (a group of people who make laws for a country), convince (to make someone believe or agree with you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: hide (to go somewhere where other people cannot see you), national assembly (a group of people who make laws for a country), fire (to make someone leave their job). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Researchers at Flinders University in Australia have discovered that new shark-bite-resistant wetsuits can significantly reduce injuries during shark attacks. These suits are made from materials containing strong fibers such as Kevlar and polyethylene, which help protect against deep cuts and blood loss. Although the suits cannot completely prevent internal injuries, they can lower the number and severity of wounds, giving victims more time to receive emergency help. Tests were done using white and tiger sharks, and the results showed that these new materials performed much better than regular neoprene. Researchers were surprised by how much damage was reduced. Shark attacks are rare, but they can be fatal , so any improvement in protection is important. Traditional chain mail suits used for diving are too heavy and inflexible for surfers, so the goal now is to make these new materials more flexible while keeping them strong enough to save lives. Difficult words: Kevlar (a strong synthetic fiber), fatal (causing death), chain mail (small metal rings linked together). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

They see that the new materials work better than normal wetsuits. Old metal suits are too heavy and hard to move in, so the team wants to make new suits that are softer and easier for surfers to use, but still very strong. Difficult words: wetsuit (a tight piece of clothing that people wear in water to keep warm and protect their body), bit e (to use your teeth to cut or injure), injury (hurt to the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
